channel.description: Latest articles from Contractor UK Limited (contractoruk.com)

item.title: IR35 & Right of Substitution in 2026/27: Explainer for Contractors
item.description: Whether it’s you or the client who sets your IR35 status, being able to send Dylan in your place is key for self-employment. Just don’t do it for the sake of it.

item.title: Post Office hit with ‘crazy’ £104million HMRC bill for IR35 failings
item.description: The Post Office Ltd becomes the public sector’s single largest off-payroll working compliance failure, ‘sending a clear message’ to the private sector that robust IR35 processes are ‘essential rather than optional.’

item.title: IR35 & Mutuality of Obligation in 2026/27: Explainer for Contractors
item.description: How a court case changes what’s now relevant to contractors trying to fight their corner on MOO.

item.title: How to run a limited company — efficiently: smarter profit strategies
item.description: Retain. Share. Plan. Contractors employing a bit of thoughtfulness over drawing out every pound possible will likely be on the money on Tuesday, too.

item.title: Here’s Joint & Several Liability’s big misconception, and 5 key risks
item.description: SafeRec says despite April fast approaching, too much of the temporary labour supply chain still thinks the risk of HMRC’s framework is only about whether the tax liability has been paid.

item.title: Unlike today’s ‘boring’ Spring Statement 2026, Make Work Pay is transformative for contractors
item.description: FCSA: With its legislative plate pretty full, the UK contractor sector must hope Rachel Reeves’ imminent statement lives up to its uneventful billing.

item.title: Spring Statement 2026: chancellor’s full speech
item.description: Rachel Reeves vows to stay the course and stick to our plan, “a plan that is more necessary than ever before in a world of uncertainty.”

item.title: Rachel Reeves overlooks contractors in ‘thin’ Spring Statement 2026
item.description: What the chancellor’s ‘not fooling anyone’ fiscal update means for contractors, according to SG Accounting, Mellor & Co, Brookson, LITRG and other UK contracting experts.

item.title: What did Spring Statement 2026 say about mortgages?
item.description: All quiet on the domestic front? The chancellor is right to say it is, but it would be wrong for contractors to wait for Middle East-infused mortgage rates.

item.title: Why the McCann Review is the latest failure of the Loan Charge scandal
item.description: LCAG: Ministers said a quick and partial review would resolve Loan Charge cases, but the McCann Review will be the latest failure of the Loan Charge scandal.
